back2basics.concept: Electoral Roll Revision and Voter Registration
back2basics.text: Electoral rolls are updated periodically to include new voters and remove ineligible ones. The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) is a process to revise electoral rolls more thoroughly. Voters can update their details using specific forms like Form 8 for address changes. The Election Commission of India oversees this process to ensure accurate and inclusive voter lists.

2026-10-18-am-1cbdc77d3c.deck: The Bombay High Court has questioned the Election Commission of India (ECI) over deletion of voter names during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. This raises important issues about voter rights, the validity of electoral rolls, and the legal procedures for updating voter information.

Such oversight strengthens democratic processes by ensuring inclusive and accurate voter registration.

back2basics.concept: Air Quality Management and Stubble Burning
back2basics.text: Air quality management involves monitoring and controlling pollutants to protect public health and the environment. Paddy stubble burning is a major source of air pollution in northern India, releasing particulate matter and harmful gases. Managing crop residue through in-situ (on-field) and ex-situ (off-field) methods, supported by machinery and enforcement, helps reduce pollution and improve air quality.

2026-10-18-am-2a8a0357ef.deck: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) conducted inspections and reviews in Punjab's districts and the National Capital Region (NCR) to assess enforcement against stubble burning and industrial pollution. This matters for UPSC aspirants as it highlights India's institutional mechanisms for air pollution control and sustainable agricultural residue management.

body.label: Inspections conducted
body.text: Between 25.09.2026 and 09.10.2026, CAQM's Enforcement Task Force conducted 124 inspections across NCR, including 54 industrial units, 6 construction and demolition sites, and 64 diesel generator sets.

body.label: Violations and actions
body.text: These inspections found 55 violations leading to proposed closures of 2 C&D projects and 3 industrial units, sealing of 12 units, and issuance of compliance orders and environmental compensation.

body.label: Flying Squads' role
body.text: CAQM's Flying Squads inspected 28,868 units across NCR, issued 1,837 closure directions, and 1,491 resumption orders after compliance verification.

body.label: Focus sectors
body.text: Inspections prioritized Red and Orange category industries, especially those with furnaces and boilers, to effectively mitigate air pollution.

body.label: Coordination and monitoring
body.text: CAQM emphasized strengthening enforcement, timely compliance verification, and close coordination among agencies for pollution control.

sections.heading: What enforcement actions did CAQM review in the NCR?

body.label: District visits and reviews
body.text: CAQM teams visited Moga, Firozpur, and Faridkot districts to assess ground-level implementation of stubble burning prevention during the paddy harvesting season.

body.label: Management measures
body.text: The Commission reviewed in-situ and ex-situ management of paddy residue, including availability and deployment of Crop Residue Management (CRM) machinery and field surveillance.

body.label: Technology use
body.text: Deployment of drones and low-cost sensors was reviewed for monitoring and trend analysis of stubble burning incidents.

body.label: Farmer facilitation
body.text: Efforts to sensitize farmers about the harmful effects of stubble burning and to facilitate their access to CRM machinery were emphasized.

body.label: Coordination among stakeholders
body.text: CAQM stressed better coordination among farmers, aggregators, industries, and district administrations to prevent stubble burning.

back2basics.text: Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) is a system under the Biological Diversity Act that ensures benefits arising from the use of biological resources are shared fairly with local communities and stakeholders. It promotes conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity by regulating commercial and research use of biological resources and distributing benefits to support local biodiversity governance and livelihoods.

2026-10-18-am-2bba93a0e5.deck: The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) distributed Rs 1.19 crore to 29 State Biodiversity Boards and one UT Biodiversity Council under the Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) mechanism to support biodiversity conservation and community welfare. This highlights the practical implementation of biodiversity governance and benefit sharing under India's Biological Diversity Act.

Inflation is the rate at which the general level of prices for goods and services rises, eroding purchasing power. Central banks like the RBI use inflation data to guide monetary policy decisions such as adjusting interest rates to maintain price stability and support economic growth.

back2basics.concept: Foreign Exchange Market and Currency Management
back2basics.text: The foreign exchange market is where currencies are traded and their values determined. Central banks like the RBI intervene to stabilize their currency by managing liquidity, regulating derivative contracts, and controlling speculative trading. Currency depreciation can increase import costs and inflation, so managing volatility is crucial for economic stability.

2026-10-18-am-a9c77722ba.deck: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) introduced regulatory measures on October 10, 2026, to manage rupee depreciation and reduce volatility in the foreign exchange market. These steps are crucial for maintaining market discipline, managing inflation, and ensuring financial stability amid external pressures.

body.label: Derivative contract restrictions
body.text: RBI barred rebooking of cancelled foreign exchange derivative contracts involving INR to curb speculative activity, while allowing rollovers on maturity.

body.text: Authorised dealers must obtain undertakings confirming that the same underlying exposure is not hedged with multiple dealers.

body.label: Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve (FERR)

body.label: Mobilising foreign capital

back2basics.concept: El Nino and its impact on monsoon
back2basics.text: El Nino is a climate phenomenon characterized by the warming of surface waters in the Pacific Ocean, which disrupts normal weather patterns globally. In India, it often leads to deficient monsoon rainfall and higher temperatures, affecting agriculture and water availability. Understanding El Nino helps explain seasonal variations and challenges in water resource management.

back2basics.text: Reservation is an affirmative action policy in India that allocates a certain percentage of government jobs and educational seats to socially and educationally backward classes. It aims to promote social equality and empowerment. The state has the authority to modify reservation policies during recruitment processes, but such changes must be transparent and not violate applicants' rights.

2026-10-18-am-e3c15e164e.deck: The Telangana High Court dismissed writ petitions challenging the State government's 2009 decision to reserve 30% of Secondary Grade Teacher posts for Diploma in Education (D.Ed.) holders. This ruling clarifies the scope of state authority in modifying reservation policies during recruitment processes, a key issue in social justice and education governance.

body: The Telangana High Court upheld the state's authority to modify reservation policies during recruitment, reinforcing the state's prerogative.
The court emphasized transparency and fairness, ensuring that changes do not deprive candidates of promised rights.
Judicial rulings help balance affirmative action goals with legal safeguards against arbitrary changes.
Such decisions impact social justice by affirming reservation benefits for marginalized groups.
structure.conclusion: Judicial review ensures reservation policies are implemented fairly, balancing state authority and candidate rights.
structure.intro: Judicial review plays a critical role in interpreting and upholding reservation policies in India.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about the Telangana High Court's 2026 ruling on reservation for D.Ed. candidates:
1. The court upheld a 30% reservation for D.Ed. candidates in Secondary Grade Teacher recruitment.
2. The reservation was introduced after the selection process had begun, which the court ruled illegal.
mcq.trap: Statement 2 is incorrect because the court ruled that the reservation was introduced at the threshold of the selection process, not after it had begun.

body.label: Reservation upheld
body.text: The Telangana High Court upheld the State government's 2009 order reserving 30% of Secondary Grade Teacher posts for candidates with a Diploma in Education (D.Ed.).

body.label: Timing of reservation change
body.text: The court observed that the reservation modification was made at the threshold of the selection process and not after it had begun, allowing the state to refine its recruitment design.

body.label: Legal challenge dismissed
body.text: Writ petitions challenging the reservation as illegal and arbitrary were dismissed, affirming the government's prerogative to modify reservation policies before the selection process concludes.

sections.heading: What was the Telangana High Court's ruling on the 30% reservation?

body.label: State's prerogative
body.text: The ruling confirms that the State cannot be denied its ordinary prerogative to modify recruitment rules before the selection process is finalized.

body.label: Limits on reservation changes
body.text: The court emphasized that changes should be made transparently and must not deprive applicants of promised rights by stealth or afterthought.

body.label: Impact on social justice
body.text: By upholding reservation for D.Ed. candidates, the judgment supports affirmative action policies aimed at empowering qualified teacher candidates from reserved categories.

sections.heading: Why does this ruling matter for reservation policy and recruitment?

body.label: Initial notification
body.text: On December 6, 2008, the undivided Andhra Pradesh government issued a notification to fill 52,655 teacher posts through District Selection Committees.

body.label: Reservation order
body.text: About a month later, the government issued an order reserving 30% of posts exclusively for D.Ed. qualification holders.

body.label: Legal challenge timeline
body.text: Candidates who failed to secure posts challenged the reservation after the written test in May 2009, but their pleas were dismissed by the AP Administrative Tribunal and later by the High Court.
